title: Draft: BT-uTP: Follow Stream
description:
Add Endpoint type for uTP connection IDs.
Manage uTP conversations and streams.
Support Follow Stream for BT-uTP, handling reordering and ACKs.
Display more information in INFO column, similar to TCP.
Move UDP address filter to header so uTP can use it.
This is some progress towards #8792.

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/4578/diffs?diff_id=260031907&start_sha=34b33bdd54f3b516ed5e64f8d302bc37aa3ab9f6)

It's useful for my analysis to be able to see and save the BitTorrent protocol level without the uTP headers, and dealing with retransmissions, reordered packets, etc. that the UDP follow stream does not. A lot of data blocks are split over multiple PDUs and are not aligned to packet starts in the stream.

The generated stream ID is definitely useful to filter out all the packets in one particular connection (since the two sides have a different but related connection ID, and its possible in some cases, especially with VPNs or NAT, to have what looks like multiple connections to the same host.)

I do think that the method of adding Follow Stream capabilities for a new protocol is clunky, spreading changes in a number of files in the ui directory, and it would be significantly cleaner to have the API be similar to that for Export PDU, where additional types could be registered dynamically with code largely in the individual dissector. The types that have substreams do make it more difficult, so that was a bigger change than I was willing to think about. There are a number of protocols that have stream like payloads that it would be useful to be able to view and save, and doing this for all of them will get unwieldy.

I can separate out the Follow parts from the other changes if that would be easier. (Still keeping the generated stream ID just to filter.)

commits_data.title: BT-uTP: Follow Stream
commits_data.message:
BT-uTP: Follow Stream

Support Follow Stream for BT-uTP, handling reordering and ACKs.
Move UDP address filter to header so uTP can use it.
Remove a little bit of the code copied from TCP that is not needed
(since uTP only carries bittorrent) to simplify things a bit.
